summary: Every-5-minute cron does KV, D1, Workers AI, R2 and Queue work for every user.

expected_findings.contains: const { results: users } = await env.DB.prepare("SELECT id, email FROM users").all<User>();
expected_findings.explanation: The cron runs 288 times a day and, for every user with no LIMIT or batching, reads KV, scans that user's full activity history in D1, runs an AI summary over all of it, writes a new R2 object, inserts a D1 row and enqueues an email. There is no change detection, and Promise.all starts every user at once. One run cannot grow without limit: D1 allows 1,000 queries per invocation, about 500 users at two queries each, and Workers AI's default limit is 300 text-generation requests a minute, so the fan-out stops growing with users after a few hundred. What keeps growing is the history: every run reads each user's full activity again, 288 times a day, and nothing stops that, so the cost rate has no limit.
